claims.claim: A one-target bottleneck reduction confines a length search to a ratio-n interval; separate all-target repetition adds n.
Ashvinkumar Theorem 1 gives deterministic all-target bicriteria time Otilde(m log(nW)/epsilon^9).
The paragraph after Theorem 2 distinguishes the open strongly polynomial all-target problem from the single-target consequence.
Ashvinkumar, Bernstein and Karczmarz make the same all-target aspect distinction.

claims.claim: The clock dynamic program and conditional-expectation witness potential originate in Ashvinkumar.
Recursive offline activation and multiplicative counting have an ordinary-SSSP precedent in Gorkiewicz and Karczmarz.
McCauley, Moseley, Niaparast, Niaparast and Singh supply an offline ordinary-SSSP precedent.
Those additive ordinary-distance results do not provide the stopped stochastic boundary contract used here.
The paper supplies a full all-input strong-polynomial all-target RSP resolution and its finite-precision, witness and total-work lemmas.
